What is claimed is true: at HEAD both switched-off arms return a scalar with has_graph FALSE whose backward raises 'element 0 of tensors does not require grad and does not have a grad_fn'; at NOW both return has_graph TRUE, value exactly 0.0, finite even when h is all-inf, backward_ok with dh_max 0.0, and the routed arm is numerically unchanged (aux 0.500643253326416 at HEAD and NOW). The report noticed the line seeds bal_acc and recorded it as a benefit ('so aux carries a graph there even in the ... case where every weighted term is off'); it is also the removal of the one detector this package has for the defect class the record type exists to name. findings.detail: THE STRUCTURE OF THE PARAGRAPH IS RIGHT AND ITS DIGITS ARE STILL CONDITIONED ON SOMETHING IT DOES NOT NAME -- which is the same defect one turn later. What reproduces exactly on my instrument at the eight widths the paragraph names: the poisoned window-6 grad|A|max is 3.1788775e-3 at the shipped FAB_SPAWN=1/FAB_AE_W=0.5 and EXACTLY 0.0 at FAB_AE_W=0, at FAB_SPAWN=0 and at both, with ONE clean value shared by all three ae-off arms -- so 'either lever removes that route' and 'the residue is the ae round trip' are both true, and the body's gate `spawn_on and ae_w > 0.0 and learn` is what they say it is. WHAT DOES NOT REPRODUCE: the grad|B| pair '1.7490769e-2 -> 7.3022917e-8'. B reaches the loss through the mixture as (hA)^T grad_out, which does not need the identity channel and does not vanish, because fabric/api.py::build draws A uniform(-1/sqrt(d), +1/sqrt(d)) and only B is zero-init. Under the objective the composition root actually backwards -- spine/compose.py:1028-1031, 'LM.lm_loss's mean + LM.anchor_term's already-weighted term + FabricOut.aux_loss + WORLD's loss' -- the same insertion at the same widths gives grad|B|max 3.0155098e-2 -> 2.3281723e-2, i.e. B KEEPS 77% of its gradient. So the two grad|B| numbers now standing in the file are true of an aux-only probe and false of a routed training pass in the composed run, and a reader will take them for the latter. Separately, the '82% of A's gradient' figure is a property of their input draw and not of the eight named widths: at those same widths I measure 87.5%. The paragraph should name the objective the numbers were backwarded through; nothing else in it needs to move.

I built the pipeline from the frozen signatures myself -- LM.resolve -> LM.build_model -> SIG.build -> FAB.build -> OPT.build, then 30 windows of LM.encode -> SIG.encode -> FAB.forward -> LM.decode -> cross-entropy + out.aux_loss -> OPT.scaled_backward -> OPT.maybe_step, one process per configuration with lever._reopen_assembly() and rng.reset_issued(). THE RETRACTED PROBE reproduces the void reading exactly on the SAME instrument: grad|A| = grad|B| = 0.0 at every one of 30 steps. Their retracted-probe dA_max needs one correction I make on my own numbers, not theirs: with FAB_SPAWN at its default the probe's dA_max is 0.25 even at OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY=0, because _spawn_check writes pop.A[slot] in place at a birth, which is not optimizer movement; with FAB_SPAWN=0 it is EXACTLY 0.0 at weight_decay=0 and 3.92422080039978e-05 at 0.01. Against that, the real run moves A by 2.0952731e-2 at weight_decay=0 with spawn off (534x) and 2.1496430e-1 with spawn on (5478x). I do not reproduce 1288.9x or 776.5x and do not quote either -- the ratio is a harness quantity at harness widths; the falsifiable shape is that the decay arm reads EXACTLY zero at zero decay while the real arm reads three to four orders of magnitude above pure decay, and that holds.
